description: Figure 5(b) is a line plot that displays the ratio of loss values for different methods relative to the Vanilla method, plotted against the number of FLOPs (floating-point operations). The x-axis, labeled "TFLOPs," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 1e7 to 9e8, with tick labels at intervals of 1e7, 2e7, 3e7, 4e8, 5e8, 6e8, 7e8, 8e8, and 9e8. The y-axis, labeled "Loss Ratio (%)," is linear and ranges from 94% to 100%. The plot contains seven distinct lines, each representing a different method: Vanilla (purple dashed line), StrmLLM (n=64) (blue dashed line), SepLLM (n=64) (orange solid line), SepLLM (n=128) (green solid line), SepLLM (n=64, H) (red solid line), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (blue solid line). All lines start near 100% at 1e7 TFLOPs and show a general downward trend as TFLOPs increase, with the Vanilla method remaining consistently at 100%. The SepLLM (n=64) line begins at approximately 97.5% and declines to around 96% by 9e8 TFLOPs. The SepLLM (n=128) line starts at approximately 97.5% and declines to around 96% by 9e8 TFLOPs. The SepLLM (n=64, H) line starts at approximately 97.5% and declines to around 96% by 9e8 TFLOPs. The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) line starts at approximately 97.5% and declines to around 96% by 9e8 TFLOPs.
